items.t: a utility page, not an area page and not a listing feed — headed "MAP SEARCH" (browser title "Map Search real estate"), it is the site's map-search utility page in name and in its own copy. There are no streets or boundaries of its own to state: the tool it describes is site-wide, spanning every area the site covers.

What a visitor actually gets (browser-verified, live visit 2026-11-01): no interactive map, no map pins, no map-specific controls and no listing results — only the two editorial blocks, the site-wide header search bar, and a "Build my search" step 1 of 5 widget, with no message that the map is hidden, unavailable or in error.

What the first editorial section actually is: not MLS® search instructions, but a short guide to reading municipal GIS maps — start with the parcel layer showing lot boundaries, click a parcel for an info window with the address, lot size and PID, then turn on zoning, OCP, ALR, flood plain and environmentally sensitive area layers, watching for setbacks and easements that shrink buildable area.

What the second editorial section claims the tool does (site copy, not verified function): an "Interactive Map Search" that lets a user search by drawing custom boundaries, filter by price, property type and features with results updating on the map, zoom from regional views to street level, save favourite searches and receive alerts when new properties match — none of which a visitor can use, because the map itself does not render for visitors: Not verified as functioning features in any other state.

Data provenance stated on the page: the MLS® Reciprocity notice naming the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® (GVR), the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board (FVREB) and the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) as the sources of the data relating to real estate on the website.

How people search for it: "map search real estate," "MLS map search," "search homes by map Fraser Valley" and by municipal GIS terms (parcel, PID, zoning map) that this page's first section also targets.

items.t: Map pins and card prices are feed data, not verified facts: any price, pin position or filter result a map tool shows is live MLS® feed data at that moment — a snapshot that changes as listings come and go — not a verified statement that a property sits inside a price band, a sub-area or a buyer's budget.

City zoning bylaw + OCP, per municipality: a site-wide map crosses many municipalities, each with its own zoning bylaw and OCP — there is no single bylaw to cite for this page, and the governing bylaw for any result is that parcel's own municipality's, verified parcel by parcel.

The ALR layer is a legal gate, not a map decoration: a parcel's Agricultural Land Reserve status is checked on the Agricultural Land Commission's maps by PID or civic address, and housing on ALR land is capped at one principal residence of 500 m² or less plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger parcels), with a secondary suite only inside the principal residence — and depositing a strata plan on ALR land is a subdivision requiring ALC permission (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)), which is why the ALR layer the page tells readers to turn on matters before a build plan is priced.

Who a listing's agent works for, for a user who finds a home and contacts its brokerage: in British Columbia, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and BCFSA states a licensed professional must only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party.

blocks.text: Good to know about Map Search

items.t: The only honest line about the map's state never reaches a visitor. "Map search hidden while editing" appears in the page's fetched text between its two editorial sections — an editing-mode artifact a visitor never sees. A visitor gets no explanation at all: no map, no pins, no results and no message, on a page whose headline promise is a map.

The page's strongest content is not a listing search at all. Its first section is a municipal GIS due-diligence guide — parcel, PID, zoning, OCP, ALR, floodplain and sensitive-area layers — which works with any city's own GIS today, map tool or no map tool; its second section describes the MLS® tool that does not render. The useful half and the broken half are different products sharing one page.
The worked example in the copy is an illustration, not a rule.

No update clock is published for the data behind the tool. A user cannot tell from the page whether a pin they are looking at is hours or days old, which is one more reason a result is a lead to verify, not a fact.
A search tool gets no market statistics, by design. The numbers a map user needs live one level down, in the city and area places the search is supposed to lead to.

The typical map user is location-first, and the page knows it. The uses its own two sections describe are location-first buyers drawing a boundary around a commute, a school area or a stretch of waterfront, and land buyers checking parcel, zoning and reserve layers before touring — the GIS half of the page serves the second group today; the first group is the one the missing map leaves unserved.

items.t: What the page is: a utility page, not an area page and not a listing feed — headed "MAP SEARCH" (browser title "Map Search real estate"), it is the site's map-search utility page in name and in its own copy. There are no streets or boundaries of its own to state: the tool it describes is site-wide, spanning every area the site covers.

The defect, precisely as the research documents it (browser-verified, live visit 2026-11-01): a live browser visit found no interactive map, no map pins, no map-specific controls and no listing results on this page. What a visitor gets is the page's two blocks of editorial copy under "Map Search" and "Interactive Map Search," plus the site-wide header search bar and a separate "Build my search" step 1 of 5 widget — and NO message saying the map is hidden, unavailable or in error. Plainly stated: the page promises a map search that is not present for visitors. Whether the tool functions in some other state (e.g., signed-in) was not tested: Not verified.

Market context: none stated for this page, deliberately. It is a site-wide utility page with no listings visible at reading and no single community; SnapStats covers exactly 14 communities with Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined splits only and medians at community level only, and SnapStats publishes no land category — attaching any community's figures to a search tool would mislead, and no detached figure is ever presented as a land figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Map Search

items.t: Zoning / OCP, per municipality: a site-wide map crosses many municipalities, each with its own zoning bylaw and OCP — there is no single bylaw to cite for this page, and the governing bylaw for any result is that parcel's own municipality's, verified parcel by parcel. What each municipality's GIS shows layer by layer, and the exact setback or easement figures for any lot: Not verified at municipal level.

ALR block, in full (the ALR layer is a legal gate, not a map decoration): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); a principal residence built without an ALC application must be 500 m² or less total floor area, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction; a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; one additional detached residence is permitted without an application at 90 m² or less (parcels of 40 ha or smaller) or 186 m² or less (larger parcels), where local bylaws also permit it. A parcel's ALR status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address.

Bare-land strata block (for any bare-land strata lot a search surfaces): Form B (SPA s.59) within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page, with rules, budget and most recent depreciation report attached; depreciation reports every 5 years for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; CRF minimum 10% since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. Fee-simple contrast: a fee-simple lot carries none of this.

Property transfer tax — the figure a map-search user is usually budgeting around: general 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000, based on fair market value at registration unless an exemption applies. Worked example, inputs + tier math stated: $800,000 fair market value, no exemption = $2,000 (1% × $200,000) + $12,000 (2% × $600,000) = $14,000. Newly Built Home Exemption: full to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000 — a new HOME, not bare land. A map's price filter does not compute this.

Who a listing's agent works for, for a user who finds a parcel and contacts its brokerage: in British Columbia, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and BCFSA states a licensed professional must only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party.
Speculation / vacancy taxes and purchase prohibition: Vancouver Empty Homes Tax (3%) is Vancouver ONLY and a region-wide map does not change that.
Schools: none stated for this page — a site-wide tool has no catchment geography.

faq.q: So where do I actually search for condos on this site?
faq.a: Those rosters, not a map pin, are the record of what stock exists where.

faq.q: Can I trust a map pin's price or its position inside my price band?
faq.a: Set the ceiling explicitly in your own search and re-check the specific listing; a building's band status is not confirmed until a live listing for it is read.

faq.q: If I find a condo through a search, what documents decide what it really costs?
faq.a: The strata package, not the card: the Form B (within 7 days of a proper request, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page) with the current depreciation report, budget, rules, CRF balance and any Rental Disclosure Statement attached — fees, approved levies, age/pet rules and insurance all live there, and a search result shows none of them.

faq.q: Then why does the fetched page text say "Map search hidden while editing"?
faq.a: That line is an editing-mode artifact in the fetched text — it is not shown to visitors.

faq.q: Can I trust a map pin's price or its position inside my price band?
faq.a: No — pins and card prices are live feed data, not verified band membership: they change as listings come and go, and no feed-freshness interval is stated for this map. Band status is not confirmed per parcel until a live listing for that parcel is read.

faq.q: What market figures describe the area this map covers?
faq.a: None are stated for this page: it is a site-wide tool covering many municipalities, SnapStats publishes figures for 14 communities only (Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined, medians at community level only) and no land category, and no single community's figures describe a region-wide search — market figures for this page are not verified / not applicable.

faq.q: Is the interactive map search working on this page?
faq.a: No — not for a visitor (browser-verified, live visit 2026-11-01): the page shows no interactive map, no pins, no map controls and no listing results — only editorial copy under "Map Search" and "Interactive Map Search" describing a map tool, the site-wide header search bar, and a "Build my search" step 1 of 5 widget. The page gives visitors no message that the map is hidden or unavailable; the line "Map search hidden while editing" appears only in the page's fetched/editing text, not on the visitor-facing page. The copy describes the intended tool (drawn boundaries, filters, alerts), not a working one.

faq.q: What layers does the page say to check on a municipal GIS map?
faq.a: The parcel layer first — lot boundaries, with an info window giving the address, lot size and PID — then zoning, OCP, ALR, flood plain and environmentally sensitive area layers, watching for setbacks and easements that shrink buildable area. That sequence is the page's own copy, reported as site copy.

faq.q: How do I check whether a lot I find is in the Agricultural Land Reserve?
faq.a: On the Agricultural Land Commission's maps, by PID or civic address. If the parcel is in the ALR, housing is generally limited to one principal residence of 500 m² or less plus at most one additional residence capped at 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), subject to local bylaws.
